title: Ranking Agreement Does Not Reveal Paragraph-Edit Agreement in Two Released Paper Acceptance Predictors
abstract: arXiv:2611.06789v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: A fast acceptance classifier could select revisions for a slower evaluator. We ask whether agreement on existing papers supports that use. We compare a classifier of word and document features with two released text-only acceptance predictors fine-tuned from the same language model with three billion parameters. For 198 papers from the International Conference on Learning Representations, we compare model rankings of the original papers and of paragraph rewrites screened automatically for unchanged facts, claim strength, and attribution. The classifier ranks original papers closely with one predictor and moderately with the other, but shows no detectable agreement with either on which rewrites raise scores. The tests specified in advance used reduced numerical precision. Rounding error dominated the small score responses. We therefore rescored the released weights in full 32-bit precision as a post hoc check; edit agreement remained near

translated_title: 排名一致性无法揭示两个已发布论文录用预测器之间的段落编辑一致性
translated_abstract: 快速的录用分类器可以为较慢的评估器筛选修改版本。我们探讨了对现有论文的排名一致性是否支持这种用途。我们将一个基于词语和文档特征的分类器与两个已发布的纯文本录用预测器进行比较，这两个预测器均从同一个拥有三十亿参数的语言模型微调而来。针对国际学习表征会议（ICLR）的198篇论文，我们比较了模型对原始论文以及对段落改写版本的排名，这些改写版本经过自动筛选，确保其事实、论点强度和引用来源保持不变。该分类器对原始论文的排名与其中一个预测器高度接近，与另一个中度一致，但在判断哪些改写会提高分数方面，与两者均无可检测到的一致性。预先设定的测试使用了降低的数值精度，舍入误差主导了微小的分数响应。因此，我们事后以完整的32位精度对已发布的权重重新打分；编辑一致性仍然接近（零）。
tldr: 研究发现，两个论文录用预测器尽管在原始论文排名上高度一致，但在判断哪些段落改写能提升分数时几乎没有一致性，且降低的数值精度产生的舍入误差会掩盖微小的分数变化。
en_tdlr: Although two paper acceptance predictors agree closely on ranking original papers, they show little agreement on which paragraph rewrites raise scores, and reduced numerical precision causes rounding errors that dominate small score responses.
